subject: general
question: A machine depreciates at a rate of 10% per annum. If the current value of the machine is ₹1,00,000, what will be its value after 2 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of depreciation = 10% = 1/10.

Multiplying factor for each year = 1 − 1/10 = 9/10.

Value after 2 years = 1,00,000 × (9/10) × (9/10)

⇒ Value = 1,00,000 × 81/100 = 81,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹81,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Value (P) = ₹1,00,000

Rate of depreciation (R) = 10% per annum

Time (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 − R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 1,00,000 × (1 − 10/100)²

⇒ A = 1,00,000 × (90/100)²

⇒ A = 1,00,000 × (9/10) × (9/10)

⇒ A = 1,00,000 × 81/100

⇒ A = 1000 × 81 = 81,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹81,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Appreciation Formula

If an item appreciates in value at R% per annum, the value after n years is given by A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ.

Successive Percentage Change

For two consecutive percentage changes x% and y%, the net percentage change is given by (x + y + xy/100)%. For 10% depreciation twice, it is (−10 − 10 + 100/100)% = −19%. Value becomes 100% − 19% = 81% of the original.

Value n Years Ago

If the current value is P and it has been depreciating at R% per annum, its value n years ago was P ÷ (1 − R/100)ⁿ.
